mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with the FEDFUNDS rate change (p > 0.05) in the identified regime, or the rate stays below 5.25% for the full horizon.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPIAUCSL monthly inflation rate exceeds 3% for two consecutive months, investors anticipate a pre-emptive rate hike by the FED, causing a sharp discount in equity valuations and a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 3% and remains above for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: No significant negative return in 20-day forward window when inflation exceeds 3% for two months, or FEDFUNDS remains unchanged during the period.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in monthly PAYEMS (labor market activity) of at least 5% for three months indicates a strengthening labor market, prompting firms to increase capital spending and drive equity market expansion, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS grows by at least 5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS growth meets the trigger, or the effect is explained by other variables (e.g., GDP growth).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO (industrial production index) of over 10% in a month signals supply-side weakness, reducing future earnings expectations and generating negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by more than 10% in a single month
failure_condition: No significant negative return when INDPRO falls >10%, or the effect is absent in non-shock months.

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (housing starts) increases by more than 15% in two consecutive months, it reflects renewed housing demand, which is associated with consumer confidence and corporate investment, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST grows by more than 15% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when HOUST meets the trigger, or the effect is mediated by other demand indicators (e.g., retail sales).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in UNRATE (unemployment rate) below 4% suggests labor market tightness, prompting the Fed to maintain a restrictive policy stance that compresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE remains below 4% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: No negative return when UNRATE stays below 4% for the horizon, or the effect is absent in non-tight labor regimes.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in PAYEMS and RSAFS (retail sales) of at least 8% in the same month indicate consumer and business demand expansion, which typically precedes equity market optimism and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: Both PAYEMS and RSAFS increase by at least 8% in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both proxies rise by at least 8%, or the effect is explained by other variables (e.g., GDP).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in GDPC1 (GDP in chained dollars) of over 2% in a quarter suggests economic contraction, which lowers growth expectations and yields negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls by more than 2% in a single quarter
failure_condition: No negative return when GDP falls >2% in a quarter, or the effect is absent in non-contraction quarters.
